specPoints.text: explain some of the uses of electromagnetic radiations, including: • radio waves: broadcasting and communications

primer.text: Every band of the electromagnetic spectrum you have ordered by wavelength also earns its keep somewhere: transmitters, ovens, cameras, hospitals. This lesson walks the bands from radio to gamma and attaches each one to its standard uses, the list examiners expect you to quote from memory.

lessons.title: Uses of EM waves
lessons.opening: Each radiation band is good at a different job, decided by how it interacts with matter. Radio and microwave carry communications, infrared warms and images in the dark, visible light feeds cameras and our eyes, ultraviolet makes lamps glow, x-rays peer through flesh to bone, and gamma rays sterilise what heat cannot reach.
keyPoints: Radio waves are used for broadcasting and communications.
Microwaves are used for cooking and satellite transmissions.
Infrared is used in heaters, night-vision equipment and remote controllers.
Visible light is used in photography, and ultraviolet in fluorescent lamps.
X-rays observe internal structure including medical uses; gamma rays sterilise food and medical equipment.

low.restatement: Each band has a signature use: radio and microwave for communications and cooking, infrared for heat and night vision, visible for images, ultraviolet for fluorescence, x-ray for seeing inside, gamma for sterilising.
low.analogy: A toolbox where each spanner fits a different nut: the bands are tools shaped by physics for particular jobs.
low.examPointer: The uses table is the examinable list; quote one use per band and name the band exactly.

medium.restatement: The uses follow from interactions: long-wave radiations carry signals around obstacles, mid-infrared couples to heat, higher-frequency bands penetrate matter or deposit energy in cells, which is why medicine splits between x-ray imaging and gamma killing.
medium.analogy: Keys cut for different locks: penetration, heating and fluorescence each unlock different applications.
medium.examPointer: Link a use to its reason when the question says explain: microwaves heat because water absorbs them; x-rays image because bone absorbs them.

check.stem: Which radiations carry broadcasting and communications?

options.explanation: Gamma sterilises; it does not broadcast.
Broadcasting and communications are the radio band uses.
Ultraviolet drives fluorescent lamps.
X-rays image internal structure.

check.stem: Microwaves are used for cooking and for:

options.explanation: That is the ultraviolet use.
Sterilising is the gamma use.
Satellite links share the microwave band with ovens.
Night vision belongs to infrared.

check.stem: Night-vision security cameras see people in the dark because they detect:

options.explanation: People do not broadcast radio.
X-ray imaging needs a source and dose, not passive body heat.
Gamma is far too energetic for body-heat imaging.
Thermal imaging works in infrared, which warm objects emit.

check.stem: Fluorescent lamps work because their coating absorbs ultraviolet and:

options.text: re-emits the energy as visible light
options.explanation: Fluorescence converts absorbed ultraviolet into visible emission.
The lamp process is absorption and re-emission, not reflection.
The energy is re-emitted, not banked.
Energy is converted, never destroyed.
Infrared heats; it is not the sterilising band here.
Radio carries signals, not sterilisation.
Gamma kills bacteria, so it sterilises food and equipment.
Visible light photographs and illuminates.

check.stem: State the use of visible light given in the uses table.
State one medical use of x-rays.
check.modelAnswer: X-ray images show the internal layout of body parts, so hospitals use them to image broken bones.

check.stem: Explain why microwaves can heat food but radio waves used for broadcasting are not used to cook.
check.modelAnswer: Microwaves at high intensity couple strongly to water in food and deposit energy as heat, while the broadcast band is chosen and regulated to carry signals without depositing useful heating energy in its surroundings.

check.stem: A hospital needs to image a broken bone and to sterilise sealed surgical tools. State which band serves each task.
check.modelAnswer: X-rays image the bone, because denser material absorbs them and reveals internal structure; gamma rays sterilise the sealed tools, because gamma kills bacteria even through packaging.

glossary.definition: Absorbing ultraviolet light and re-emitting it as visible light, making a substance glow.
To kill bacteria and other microbes on equipment or food.
The named regions of the electromagnetic spectrum, from radio waves to gamma rays.
